findings.title: Race condition allows a single backup code to authenticate multiple concurrent logins
findings.body: In the backup code branch the lookup is `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` followed by `backupCodes[index] = null` and a plain `prisma.user.update` that re‑encrypts the array. Two concurrent requests that both submit the same valid backup code can both read the same index, both set it to null, and both `update` the row. The result is two authenticated sessions for one single‑use code. The lookup/mutation needs to be wrapped in a transaction with a row-level lock (or otherwise made atomic, e.g. by storing a hash plus a per-code marker) so that the second concurrent attempt fails with `IncorrectBackupCode`. The same race exists for any caller that re-uses a code in parallel.

findings.title: Backup code login and backup-code disable paths have no e2e coverage
findings.body: The PR adds the entire backup-code feature (login flow, display, copy/download, disabling 2FA via backup code) but the e2e test only exercises the TOTP login and TOTP‑based disable. The `// TODO: add more backup code tests` comment confirms the gap. There is no test that (a) re-logs in using a generated backup code via the `Lost access` button, (b) disables 2FA with a backup code, or (c) verifies that a used backup code can no longer authenticate. These are the core acceptance criteria for the issue and must be covered before merging.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case sensitive and can fail for valid hex codes
findings.body: `backupCodes` is produced by `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, which is lowercase. The lookup compares `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` against the array with `indexOf` without normalising case, and `next-auth-options.ts` does the same. A user who copy‑pastes or types the code with uppercase letters (e.g. via autofill, or because the UI only displays a placeholder pattern `XXXXX-XXXXX` and the user assumes either case works) will be rejected with `IncorrectBackupCode` even though the code is correct. Normalise both sides to lowercase before comparing.

findings.title: No protection against malformed/corrupted `backupCodes` ciphertext
findings.body: The handler does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY))` with no try/catch. If the stored ciphertext is corrupted, the JSON is invalid, or the encryption key was rotated without re-encrypting old values, the exception bubbles up as a 500 with no actionable error. The login handler in `next-auth-options.ts` has the same shape. Wrap the decrypt+parse in try/catch and return `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` (or a new dedicated error) so the UI can show a sensible message and so the failure mode is not a generic 500.

findings.title: `resetState` leaves backup codes, secret, QR data URI and the object URL in state
findings.body: `resetState` only clears `password`, `errorMessage` and `step`. It does not clear `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri` or `secret`. The `cancel` button at lines 224-230 calls `resetState()` then closes the modal, but because the dialog is controlled (state persists while `open` toggles), a subsequent re-open of the modal can briefly render the previous user's QR/secret/backup codes while the new password-confirm step is shown, or the `backupCodesUrl` Blob URL keeps pointing at stale data. Reset all of the 2FA-related state in `resetState` and revoke `backupCodesUrl` with `URL.revokeObjectURL` before clearing it.

findings.title: `backupCodesUrl` Blob is never revoked when the modal is closed
findings.body: `setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))` is created on setup success and only revoked when `handleSetup` is invoked again. If the user closes the dialog without going through setup a second time, the Blob URL stays alive until the page unloads, holding the plaintext backup codes in memory. Call `URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)` in a cleanup effect (and in `resetState`) so the Blob is released deterministically.

findings.title: Cancel handler invokes `onCancel` before resetting local state
findings.body: The cancel button calls `onCancel()` and then `resetState()`. The parent is likely to hide the modal (or unmount the page) in response to `onCancel`, which can race with the second `resetState()` call and leave the component in a partially reset condition. Reverse the order: `resetState()` then `onCancel()`. The same pattern issue applies to the backup-codes close button at lines 266-269 (`onEnable()` before `resetState()`).

findings.title: `formatBackupCode` is referenced before its declaration
findings.body: `handleSetup` (line 77) references `formatBackupCode` inside its body, but `formatBackupCode` is declared with `const` at line 163, below the function definition. It works at runtime because `handleSetup` only runs after the component has rendered, but the order is confusing and tools that analyse temporal dead zones / eslint `no-use-before-define` will complain. Move the `formatBackupCode` definition above `handleSetup`.

findings.title: Password field in disable modal is rendered without a label
findings.body: The `PasswordField` is given `labelProps={{ className: "block text-sm font-medium text-default" }}` but no `label` prop, so `PasswordField` falls back to no label text and the styling from `labelProps` has nothing to attach to. Users opening the "Disable 2FA" dialog see an unlabeled text field and may not understand they must re-enter their account password. Pass `label={t("password")}` (matching what `EnableTwoFactorModal` does) so the dialog is self-explanatory.

findings.title: `<Label>` is not associated with the input via `htmlFor`
findings.body: The `Label` element renders the `t("backup_code")` string but has no `htmlFor` attribute, while the `TextField` declares `id="backup-code"`. Screen readers will not announce them as related and clicking the label text will not focus the input. Add `htmlFor="backup-code"` to the `Label`.

findings.title: `TextField` length attributes ignore the dash in the middle
findings.body: `minLength={10}` / `maxLength={11}` describe the raw character count, but the field is also visually presented as `XXXXX-XXXXX` and the server strips dashes before comparing (`replaceAll("-", "")`). Users may legitimately type 11 characters including the dash and be exactly at the limit, which is fine, but the placeholder and helper text never explain that the dash is optional. Either accept input with or without the dash consistently (currently accepted on the server but the length limits are tight against the user's expectation) or document/format the input so the count is obvious. Also, `required` plus `minLength={10}` makes the HTML5 validity message "Please lengthen this text to 10 characters or more (you are currently using X characters)" which is technically wrong for the dashed form (11 with dash, 10 without). Consider deriving the limits from the formatted length (11) and normalising before validation.

findings.title: Backup-code branch bypasses password verification when `totpCode` is also present
findings.body: Password verification is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`, so any request that includes a non-empty `totpCode` skips password validation entirely. The backup-code branch then takes priority over the TOTP branch (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`). An attacker who has obtained a valid backup code (e.g. by shoulder-surfing the setup screen, by stealing the user's download, or via the race condition above) can simply include any non-empty string as `totpCode` together with the backup code, and password verification is skipped. Either verify the password whenever a password is set regardless of `totpCode`, or restrict the backup-code branch so it only runs when password has already been verified.
